{{Top|rwm|can|fotj}} {{TelevisionEpisode |image=[[File:Epguide309.png]] |title="Hunt for Ziro" |series=''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars]]''{{SWArchive|url=theclonewars/guide/episode309.html|text=''The Clone Wars'' Episode Guide: Hunt for Ziro}} |season=[[The Clone Wars: Season Three|Three]] |episode=9 |production=3.05 |screener= |airdate=[[November 12]], [[2010]] |intl release= |runtime=24 minutes |director=[[Steward Lee]] |writer=*[[Steve Mitchell]] *[[Craig Van Sickle]] |production company= |guests= |canon_timeline=[[21 BBY]]{{TCWcanondates|309}} |legends_timeline=[[20 BBY/Legends|20 BBY]]{{TCWdates|309}} |prev="[[Evil Plans]]" |next="[[Heroes on Both Sides]]"{{InsiderCite|121|Launchpad}} }} {{Quote|Love comes in all shapes and sizes.|Moral|{{TCW|Hunt for Ziro}}}} "'''Hunt for Ziro'''" is the ninth episode of the ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars]]'' television series' [[The Clone Wars: Season Three|third season]]. It aired on [[November 12]], [[2010]]. The episode is a sequel to "[[Hostage Crisis]]." ==Official description== ''Cad Bane has broken Ziro the Hutt out of prison and the Hutt Council demands that Ziro tell them where he's hidden vital -- and incriminating -- information: a journal detailing the criminal activities of the five Hutt families. Ziro makes another daring escape with the help of his estranged (and strange) lover, Sy Snootles. Bane is back on the Hutt's trail -- but he's not the only one. The Jedi Obi-Wan Kenobi and Quinlan Vos need to find him too.'' ''A chase through the swamps of Nal Hutta leads the pursuers to Ziro's enormous mother, Mama the Hutt, who points them to the direction of Teth. It is here, in the secret grave of Ziro's father, that the fugitive Hutt has hidden the diary. When he retrieves it, Snooty reveals her true spots. She's a deadly woman scorned and a bounty hunter for hire. She kills Ziro, and returns the journal to her client: Jabba the Hutt''. ==Opening narration== {{OpeningCrawl |name=Episode 9
HUNT FOR ZIRO |text=A great escape! Cad Bane and his notorious crew of bounty hunters liberated Ziro the Hutt from a Republic prison after holding the Galactic Senate hostage. The Jedi Council has assigned Obi-Wan Kenobi to retrieve Ziro the Hutt with the help of Jedi Knight Quinlan Vos. Unknown to the Jedi, we find Ziro in the clutches of the five Hutt families on the distant world of Nal Hutta....}} ==Plot summary== {{Quote|Looks as though we're not the only ones after Ziro.|Obi-Wan Kenobi|}} Following his liberation by [[Cad Bane]], [[Ziro Desilijic Tiure|Ziro the Hutt]] has been brought to the swampy [[Hutt]] home world of [[Nal Hutta]], since he is holding critically incriminating information about the Hutt [[Crime lord]]s, stored in a [[holodiary]] whose location only he knows. Ziro ensures his own safety by claiming that if something happens to him, the information would be immediately sent to the Republic authorities. However, Ziro has an ally in the singer [[Sy Snootles]], with whom he had entertained a romantic relationship. After learning that Ziro is being held captive in the Hutt stronghold, she secretly visits him. Ziro exploits her affection for him to have her break him out, and the two escape into the swamps, to the abode of [[Mama]] the Hutt, Ziro's grotesque mother, who provides him with a [[starship]] so he can travel to [[Teth]]. On [[Coruscant]], [[Obi-Wan Kenobi|Obi-Wan]] is entrusted by the [[Jedi High Council|Jedi Council]] with the task of retrieving Ziro and bringing Cad Bane to justice with the help of the skilled, but rather free-minded, crazy and impulsive [[Jedi Master]] [[Quinlan Vos]], whose company is not exactly a delight for Obi-Wan. Nevertheless, Vos is well-informed about the possible reason why Ziro has been freed, so they travel to Nal Hutta. The [[Grand Hutt Council|Hutt Council]] denies any knowledge of Ziro's and Bane's whereabouts, and Obi-Wan is reluctant to confront them openly since the [[Galactic Republic|Republic]] owes the Hutts for [[Star Wars: The Clone Wars (film)|their contributions to the war effort]], but Vos states that they could have freed him, to [[Gardulla Besadii the Elder|Gardulla's]] resentment. He then detects Ziro's presence by [[Psychometry|psychometrically]] scanning a cup Ziro has drunk from. As the two arrive at Ziro's detention cell, they find him already missing and promptly attempt to track him down. Shortly afterward, the Hutt Council also learns of Ziro's flight, and once more Cad Bane offers his services (for a fee) to retrieve the renegade Hutt. The two parties successively follow Ziro's trail to Mama's abode and learn of his intent to get to Teth. In the meantime, Ziro and Sy retrieve the diary from its hiding place, the grave of [[Papa|Ziro's father]], but then Sy, out of greed and a grudge against Ziro for having abandoned her, turns on the Hutt and blasts him to death. The Jedi and Bane meet beside the corpse and immediately begin to slug it out between themselves: While Obi-Wan intends to bring Bane to justice for the [[Hostage Crisis|Senate hostage incident]], Bane is tempted by the reward for each dead Jedi delivered to the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems|Separatists]]. The Jedi press Bane hard, however, and he barely manages to get away with his innate skills and the help of his [[droid]] aid [[Todo 360|Todo]]. But while this is going on, Sy delivers Ziro's holo-diary to her [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure|true master]]... ==Development== ===Conception=== {{Quote|Quinlan Vos was in an early draft of Bombad Jedi. He was working undercover and actually using his force abilities to make it look like Jar Jar WAS a Jedi. Jar Jar was even fooled himself for a while.|Henry Gilroy|{{WebCite|url=http://theforce.net/jedicouncil/interview/henrygilroyanddavefiloni.asp|text=Interviews - Face To Face With The Masters|work=[[TheForce.net]]|archivedate=20130723175134}}}} [[File:Quinlanconceptart.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Concept art of Quinlan Vos]] The idea of using Quinlan Vos in the animated television series ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars]]'' came from writer [[Henry Gilroy]] as early as [[2005]], soon after he became attached to the show.{{JCFCite|url=posts/29630425|board=Star Wars TV|thread=TheForce.Net interviews Henry Gilroy... and Dave Filoni !!! (Your questions answered!)|user=[[Henry Gilroy|HGilroy]]|date=2008-12-30|time=10:34 AM|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20170207114253/http://boards.theforce.net/threads/theforce-net-interviews-henry-gilroy-and-dave-filoni-your-questions-answered.29628723}} Vos was a fan-favorite{{WebCite|url=http://www.examiner.com/article/exclusive-preview-of-quinlan-vos-on-next-weeks-clone-wars|text=Exclusive preview of Quinlan Vos on next weeks Clone Wars|author=Bryan Young|date=2010-11-04|work=Examiner.com|archivedate=20140321155622}} [[Star Wars Legends|Expanded Universe]] character who had appeared in numerous issues of [[Dark Horse Comics]]' ''[[Star Wars: Republic]]'' series, though his original character design came from a background extra in the [[1999]] film [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'']]. Gilroy contacted [[John Ostrander]], who had penned most of ''Republic''{{'s}} Vos-centric issues,''[[Star Wars: Twilight]]''''[[Star Wars: Darkness]]''''[[Star Wars: Rite of Passage]]''''[[Star Wars: Republic: Siege of Saleucami]]'' to ask if he would be interested in writing the episode which featured the character's first appearance. However, the producers of ''The Clone Wars'' ultimately decided to employ experienced television animation writers early in the show's production, and Ostrander's involvement was nixed. Vos was written into an early draft of the show's [[The Clone Wars: Season One|season one]] episode "[[Bombad Jedi]]," but was cut due to limitations involving how many new character models a single episode could introduce. His first appearance thus did not come until the [[The Clone Wars: Season Three|season three]] episode "Hunt for Ziro," which drew on his character traits from the ''Republic'' [[Star Wars comic books|comics]], including his powers of psychometry and his tendency to bend the rules of the Jedi Order. Various pieces of concept art were created for the episode, including art of Vos, Vos's gunship, the swamp speeder, Mama the Hutt's home, the musical number performed by Sy Snootles, and various locations on both Teth and Nal Hutta. A maquette of Mama was also built.{{SW|url=explore/the-clone-wars/ep309|text="Hunt for Ziro" - ''The Clone Wars'' Episode Guide|nolive=1}} ===Production=== {{Quote|The dance number in the episode was inspired by the opening scene of ''Indiana Jones and the Temple of Doom'' (1984), where Willie Scott and a troupe of chorus girls entertain gangster Lao Che and his henchmen.|"Hunt for Ziro"{{'s}} episode guide|}} [[File:Anythinggoes.jpg|thumb|right|300px|The episode's dance number was inspired by a similar scene from ''Indiana Jones and the Temple of Doom''.]] "Hunt for Ziro" drew inspiration from various sources. Mama was partially inspired by the obese vampire Pearl from the [[1998]] film [[Wikipedia:Blade (film)|''Blade'']]; the [[Ran-D housekeeper droid/Legends|Ran-D housekeeper droids]] in Mama's hut were an homage to the [[1987]] film [[Wikipedia:Batteries Not Included (film)|''Batteries Not Included'']]; and when Ziro dies, he says "What a world, what a world!" in reference to a line spoken by the [[Wikipedia:Wicked Witch of the West|Wicked Witch of the West]] in [[1930s|1939's]] [[Wikipedia:The Wizard of Oz (1939 film)|''The Wizard of Oz'']]. Additionally, the musical number in Gardulla's palace was a tribute to the [[w:c:indianajones:Anything Goes|opening scene]] of [[1984]]'s [[w:c:indianajones:Indiana Jones and the Temple of Doom|''Indiana Jones and the Temple of Doom'']]. The number was inserted into the episode as a throwback to the Chicago nightclub scenes often seen in [[Wikipedia:Mob film|gangster films]]. Designer [[Darren Marshall]] and Supervising Director [[Dave Filoni]] designed the headdresses worn by Snootles's backup dancers; the headdresses have been compared to those found in Director [[Wikipedia:Julie Taymor|Julie Taymor's]] staging of [[Wikipedia:The Lion King (musical)|''The Lion King'' musical]].{{InsiderCite|125|50 Great Reasons to Rewatch Star Wars: The Clone Wars Season Three|50 Great Reasons to Rewatch ''Star Wars: The Clone Wars'' Season Three}} Originally, Jabba the Hutt was intended to be present in the palace along with his [[protocol droid]], [[TC-70]]. He was replaced by Gardulla late in the episode's production, and TC-70 was swapped for Gardulla's droid [[MF-80]]. In [[May]] [[2010]], Dan Curto of [[Rebelscum.com]] reported a rumor that Quinlan Vos would be included in ''The Clone Wars''{{'}} season three action figure line.{{Rebelscum|url=story/front/Rumor_Report_The_Clone_Wars_Basic_Figures_131216.asp|text=Rumor Report: The Clone Wars Basic Figures|author=Dan Curto|date=2010-05-11}} An image of Vos's [[Hasbro]] figure was first spotted by [http://www.yakface.com Yakface.com] in [[August]] of the same year,{{WebCite|url=http://www.eucantina.net/archives/8050|text=Quinlan Vos to Appear in ''The Clone Wars''|author=Austin|date=2010-08-23|work=EUCantina.net|archivedate=20131011101148}} and images of the character were used in official promotional materials for the series in the subsequent months.{{Blogspot|subdomain=starwarsaficionado|url=2010/10/clone-wars-coming-soon-quinlan-vos.html|name=Star Wars Aficionado|text="THE CLONE WARS" COMING SOON: QUINLAN VOS|date=2010-10-25}} An official preview of "Hunt for Ziro" was included in the [[Star Wars Insider 121|121st issue]] of ''[[Star Wars Insider]]'' magazine ([[October]] 2010), consisting of several still images and a brief plot summary. Additionally, three official preview clips were released online by [[Lucasfilm]] and the [[Cartoon Network]].{{WebCite|url=http://www.eucantina.net/archives/9411|text=Preparing for The Clone Wars: Hunt for Ziro|author=Austin|date=2010-11-12|work=EUCantina.net|archivedate=20101228061832}} "Hunt for Ziro" aired on the Cartoon Network on [[November 12]], 2010. It featured one voice actor who had never worked on ''The Clone Wars'' before: [[Al Rodrigo]] as Quinlan Vos. The episode was posted on [[StarWars.com]] three days later,{{WebCite|url=http://www.theforce.net/latestnews/story/TCW_Hunt_For_Ziro_Now_Online_134942.asp|text=''TCW: "Hunt For Ziro"'' Now Online|author=Mike|date=2010-11-15|work=[[TheForce.net]]|archivedate=20111104031236}} and was later included in [[Star Wars: The Clone Wars The Complete Season Three|''Star Wars: The Clone Wars'': The Complete Season Three]], which was released on [[October 18]], [[2011]].[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars The Complete Season Three|''Star Wars: The Clone Wars'' The Complete Season Three]] ==Release and reception== ''Star Wars'' author [[Pablo Hidalgo]] revealed that he loved both the episode and ''Star Wars'' dark comedies in general.{{WebCite|url=http://clubjade.net/?p=24311#comment-17715|text=The Clone Wars review: 'Hunt for Ziro' - comments|author=[[Pablo Hidalgo|Pabawan]]|date=2010-11-19|work=[[Tracy Duncan|Club Jade]]|archivedate=20110131013305}} [[Jan Duursema]], an artist who had collaborated with Ostrander on many of ''Republic''{{'s}} Vos-centric issues, responded positively to the character's appearance in ''The Clone Wars'', naming the showcasing of his flair for the dramatic and his interactions with Kenobi as highlights of an enjoyable episode.{{JCFCite|url=posts/31380839|board=Literature|thread=The Official Jan Duursema Discussion Thread|user=[[Jan Duursema|Jan_Duursema]]|date=2010-11-17|time=6:22 PM|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150927054639/http://boards.theforce.net/threads/the-official-jan-duursema-discussion-thread.5915607/page-96}}{{DHBoards|url=viewtopic.php?p=249277&sid=d4f5a03c94d5686ab19ab41cd1ee27e2#p249277|thread=Quinlan Vos in The Clone Wars. Please limit your whining|user=[[Jan Duursema|jan duursema]]|date=2010-11-03|time=07:39}} ''Star Wars'' author [[Daniel Wallace]] saw a discrepancy between the two depictions of Vos, however, calling the ''Republic'' version "brooding and stoic" and ''The Clone Wars''{{'}} version as "an overenthusiastic bull in a china shop."{{Blogspot|subdomain=geekosity|url=2012/03/endnotes-for-star-wars-book-of-sith_30.html|name=Daniel Wallace's Geekosity|text=Endnotes for Star Wars: Book of Sith (part 3)}} Before the episode aired, Ostrander stated that a potentially alternate take on Vos was within the purview of ''Star Wars'' creator [[George Lucas]], who ultimately owned the character. Like Duursema, he was pleased to see one of his comic book characters make the jump to ''Star Wars'' television. In [[April]] 2011, the [[Star Wars Insider 125|125th issue]] of ''Star Wars Insider'' included an article titled [[50 Great Reasons to Rewatch Star Wars: The Clone Wars Season Three|''50 Great Reasons to Rewatch'' Star Wars: The Clone Wars ''Season Three'']], written by Daniel Wallace, Pablo Hidalgo, and Leland Chee. "Hunt for Ziro" contributed six items—more than any other episode—to the list: Quinlan Vos's rudeness and the script's ''The Big Lebowski'' reference; the sensational musical number; the presence of a mummified Hutt; the slyness of Sy Snootles; the battle between Bane, Kenobi, and Vos; and the outrageous character of Mama the Hutt. ==Continuity== {{Quote|Gardulla's krayt dragon found her… indigestible.|Leland Chee, explaining Gardulla the Hutt's appearance in the episode|{{Twitter|HolocronKeeper|status/3269273187254272|[[Leland Chee]]|date=2010-11-12|quote=Gardulla's krayt dragon found her...indigestible.|archiveurl=https://archive.is/FkQrf|nolive=1}}}} In addition to using Quinlan Vos and his psychometric powers, "Hunt for Ziro" drew on other elements of the Expanded Universe as well—the Hutt homeworld of Nal Hutta has existed in ''Star Wars'' lore since as early as [[1993]]'s ''[[Dark Empire Sourcebook]]''.''[[Dark Empire Sourcebook]]'' The names of the Hutt family leaders present on Nal Hutta in the episode were revealed in "Hunt for Ziro"'s StarWars.com episode guide, although they had already appeared in [[Hologram/Legends|holographic]] form in the previous episode, "[[Evil Plans]]."{{TCW|Evil Plans}} Also revealed were the names of some of the creatures seen on Nal Hutta and one that sits atop the head of [[Marlo/Legends|Marlo the Hutt]]. The episode marks the first appearance of Sy Snootles in ''The Clone Wars''; Snootles originally appeared on the screen in the [[1983]] film [[Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi|''Star Wars'': Episode VI ''Return of the Jedi'']].{{Film|VI}} Snootles' lover, on the other hand, dies and is seen onscreen for the last time—Ziro had been a supporting character since the [[2008]] release of the [[Star Wars: The Clone Wars (film)|''Star Wars: The Clone Wars'' film]].[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars (film)|''Star Wars: The Clone Wars'' film]] [[File:GardullasDeath.jpg|thumb|left|250px|"Hunt for Ziro" retconned Gardulla the Hutt's death in the video game ''Star Wars: Bounty Hunter''.]] Another Hutt who appears in "Hunt for Ziro" is [[Gardulla Besadii the Elder/Legends|Gardulla Besadii the Elder]], despite having previously been fed to a [[Krayt dragon/Legends|krayt dragon]] in the [[2002]] [[Star Wars video games|video game]] ''[[Star Wars: Bounty Hunter]]'', which is set prior to the Clone Wars.''[[Star Wars: Bounty Hunter]]'', level 15: Gardulla's Palace After "Hunt for Ziro" aired, Leland Chee declared that the krayt dragon had found Gardulla "indigestible," echoing a similar line spoken by [[Boba Fett/Legends|Boba Fett]] in a [[1992]] [[Dark Empire 4|issue]] of the comic series ''[[Star Wars: Dark Empire]]''.[[Dark Empire 4|''Dark Empire'' 4]] However, ''Star Wars'' author [[Adrick Tolliver]] pointed out that continuity errors surrounding Gardulla's death had existed for some time, with both the [[Galactic Phrase Book & Travel Guide (real-life book)|''Galactic Phrase Book & Travel Guide'']] and the novel ''[[Tatooine Ghost]]'' mentioning her as being alive after the events of ''Bounty Hunter''.{{JCFCite|url=posts/31355646|board=Literature|thread=Clone Wars Continuity Discussion (Spoilers Allowed)|user=[[Adrick Tolliver|TalonCard]]|date=2010-11-06|time=9:39 PM|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20200802121624/https://boards.theforce.net/threads/clone-wars-continuity-discussion-spoilers-allowed.28450104/page-197}} Chronologically, the events of "Hunt for Ziro" immediately follow the events of "[[Hostage Crisis]]," an episode from ''The Clone Wars''{{'s}} first season.{{TCW|Hostage Crisis}} Together with "Evil Plans," which is set just prior to "Hostage Crisis," the three episodes form a story arc that tells the tale of Ziro's escape from a Republic prison. Their viewing order was confirmed in the [[2012]] reference book ''[[Star Wars: The Ultimate Visual Guide: Updated and Expanded]]'', which also places the comic story arc ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars: In Service of the Republic]]'' at just after "Hunt for Ziro."''[[Star Wars: The Ultimate Visual Guide: Updated and Expanded]]'', p. 72-73 ("The Hutt Contract") In [[March]] [[2014]], Keeper of the ''Star Wars'' [[Holocron continuity database]] [[Leland Chee]] revealed the chronological episode order of ''The Clone Wars''{{'s}} six seasons in a tweet, and the information was later posted in a StarWars.com blog entry. Both confirm that "Hunt for Ziro" follows "Hostage Crisis," with season three's tenth episode, "[[Heroes on Both Sides]]," being the next episode of the show in the timeline.{{Twitter|HolocronKeeper|status/443106707472801793|[[Leland Chee]]|date=2014-03-10|quote=216 116 T 301 303 101-115 117-121 201-203 217-219 204-214 220-222 305-307 302 304 308 122 309-311 215 Finding Snooty's Bracelet." ==Legacy== Quinlan Vos went on to appear in just one additional episode of ''The Clone Wars'': the [[The Clone Wars: The Lost Missions|sixth season]] episode "[[Destiny (The Clone Wars)|Destiny]]," as one of many Jedi gathered around Coruscant's Jedi Temple in a [[Force vision/Legends|vision]] experienced by Jedi Master [[Yoda/Legends|Yoda]].{{TCW|Destiny (The Clone Wars)}} He also appears in the [[Star Wars: Clone Wars Adventures (video game)|''Star Wars: Clone Wars Adventures'']] MMORPG.[[Star Wars: Clone Wars Adventures (video game)|''Star Wars: Clone Wars toyline]].{{HasbroCite|set=Star Wars: The Clone Wars (toy line)|packtype=2010 Basic Figure|pack=#36: Quinlan Vos|altlink=https://www.rebelscum.com/TCW36-QuinlanVos.asp}} ==Media==
